title: Quiet character conflict
prompt: Two longtime friends repair a radio after one has broken a promise. Let the scene remain quiet unless the characters themselves change its temperature.

title: Action without compulsory quips
prompt: A courier crosses a collapsing footbridge while protecting a sealed parcel. Keep the physical problem legible and let humor occur only if it fits.

title: Romance with direct feeling
prompt: One character admits they missed the other during a mundane grocery trip. Direct emotional language is welcome when natural.

title: Horror in an empty house
prompt: A locksmith enters a house whose front door keeps relocking behind them. Build horror from concrete events without requiring a reveal.

title: Comedy from a bad presentation
prompt: A town planner must present a disastrous slideshow to three patient residents. Let comedy arise from character and circumstance.

title: Mystery in a false inventory
prompt: A museum registrar finds an object listed in two rooms at once. Preserve uncertainty and do not solve the mystery immediately.

title: Ensemble kitchen scene
prompt: Four housemates cook during a power outage, each pursuing a different small goal. No one character must organize the whole scene.

title: A neighbor causes the change
prompt: The viewpoint character watches a neighbor independently decide to close the community garden for the night.

title: A scene that need not advance plot
prompt: Two siblings fold laundry and compare the strange pockets in old coats. The scene may simply deepen their texture.

title: Plainly stated grief
prompt: A character tells their cousin they are sad after selling a family piano. Do not require physical symptoms to validate the feeling.

title: Aftermath cleanup
prompt: After a neighborhood festival, volunteers collect cups and untie banners. Focus on aftermath without inventing a new crisis.

title: A subplot can stay dormant
prompt: During a train ride, an old unanswered letter remains in a character's bag while the immediate conversation concerns breakfast.

title: Information remains withheld
prompt: A mechanic knows why the engine failed but chooses not to explain yet. Keep the knowledge boundary without teasing it theatrically.

title: An unresolved consequence
prompt: A council has approved a noisy night market; nearby tenants discuss what may happen next without settling the issue.

title: Argument without weather mirroring
prompt: Two scientists disagree in a bright, comfortable cafeteria. Keep the setting factual rather than making it echo their emotions.

title: Conversation without gesture substitution
prompt: A tired nurse plainly declines an invitation. The response need not translate every feeling into glances, breaths, or hand movements.

title: An ordinary opening
prompt: Open with a baker already counting change for a familiar customer. No cinematic establishing shot or interruption is required.

title: An earned interruption
prompt: A solemn rehearsal is interrupted by a goat that genuinely belongs on the farm. Let the interruption matter without turning it into a twist.

title: An ambiguous apology
prompt: A former teammate says, 'I should have called.' Leave room for more than one interpretation without making all language cryptic.

title: A resolved ending
prompt: End a short scene after a child successfully returns a lost library book. A clean resolution is preferable to a compulsory hook.
